data.body:
AC2/AC3/AC4 — SWEEP EXECUTED AND VERIFIED (2026-08-13 01:16:16Z)

AC2 — run-level equality gate held. `rebar tracker-maintenance --status` re-run immediately
before any write reported `unpushed ticket commits: 0`, `stranded index entries: 0`, and a
`foreign top-level paths` list of exactly 8, byte-equal to the 8 triaged ids (sorted compare,
no diff). Because `--clean` is all-or-nothing over that set (it iterates the whole foreign
list and `shutil.rmtree`s each, with no per-directory filter), this equality assertion is the
only way to bound what it deletes — and it held, so no 9th path was in scope.

A NOTE ON A FIRST, ABORTED ATTEMPT: an earlier invocation of this same gate ABORTED with zero
writes. The cause was environmental, not a real mismatch — `rebar` was invoked with the
tracker worktree itself as cwd, which fails store attachment ("'tickets' is already used by
worktree"), so `--status` returned an error instead of a list and the equality check correctly
refused to proceed. Re-run from the throwaway checkout it passed. Recorded because the
fail-closed behaviour is the desired one: a gate that cannot read the current state must not
authorize a delete.

AC3 — removal succeeded. `rebar tracker-maintenance --clean` reported
`repaired: 0 stranded, 8 foreign path(s) removed`.
  backup ref : refs/rebar-maintenance/20260813T011616Z
  rollback   : git reset --hard refs/rebar-maintenance/20260813T011616Z
  audit      : .tickets-tracker/.git/rebar-maintenance-audit.jsonl
The break-glass `--force` was NOT used and was not needed (0 unpushed ticket commits).
All 8 directories are confirmed absent from the filesystem.

BEFORE / AFTER fsck:
    before : 16 issues = 8 MISSING_CREATE + 6 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED + 1 FOREIGN_STORE_PATH
                         + 1 ENV_ID_MISMATCH
    after  :  7 issues = 6 STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED + 1 ENV_ID_MISMATCH
    delta  : -8 MISSING_CREATE, -1 FOREIGN_STORE_PATH; nothing else changed
`rebar fsck 2>&1 | grep -c -E 'MISSING_CREATE|FOREIGN_STORE_PATH'` returns 0.

The 7 remaining findings are the two classes deliberately left alone: STATUS_FORK_RESOLVED
(benign, already auto-resolved by the reducer) and ENV_ID_MISMATCH (known by-design flag from
change 1638). Neither was touched.

AC4 — no committed data modified. Tracker HEAD captured immediately before and immediately
after `--clean`, with no intervening ticket write:
    HEAD before : cc783205d744f426011ccdafb0a4a14cd16831df
    HEAD after  : cc783205d744f426011ccdafb0a4a14cd16831df   (identical)
`git status --porcelain` on the tracker: 0 lines, before and after. This is the expected
result and the reason the operation is safe — the removed directories were empty and
uncommitted, so git had nothing to track and no commit could reference them. Nothing was
removed from history; only untracked working-tree residue was cleared.

(HEAD does advance across the ticket's own event writes — create/claim/comment/close all
auto-commit. The assertion above is deliberately scoped to the `--clean` call itself, which is
what AC4 is about: the sweep must not alter committed ticket data.)
